bpmStatus: DISPUTED — must be resolved by measurement before any lesson ships

bpmCandidates.note: Two research passes disagree by roughly a factor of two. R1 reported 89-100; the harvest pass found 160-180 rising to 200-220 in the instructors' own material, and even a single source (RF Dance) contradicts itself across two of its own articles. The likely cause is that the two passes measured different quantities: salsa's quick-quick-slow places three steps across four musical beats, so a 'step feel' rate and a musical beat rate differ by about 2x.
bpmCandidates.whyItMatters: The beat grid must run at the rate the dancer actually steps to. Getting it wrong by 2x does not produce slightly-off timing — it produces a grid that lines up with every other beat, so half the learner's correct steps are scored as misses and the product blames them for its own error.
bpmCandidates.resolution: G1: take one known track, tap-annotate it with tools/beat_annotate.py, and compare the fitted BPM against both candidate ranges. One measurement settles it; no further research round is warranted.

copyright.basis: Social dance; core shines such as Suzy Q trace to the 1930s and are public domain. Shines are by definition the solo, partnerless subset of the dance — the product's constraint matches the form rather than fighting it.
copyright.boundary: Named instructor routines are not reproduced; combos are our own arrangement of public step vocabulary.

honesty.$comment: K10 (plan §22) in machine-readable form: what this style grades, what it deliberately shows without grading, and WHY — every line traceable to a measurement, not a policy preference. Shown to the user; the app must not grade anything absent from `measured`.
measured: Leg shape through the step cycle — 8 leg joints (hips, knees, thighs, shins) agreed to within 1.57-5.76deg across 3 independent instructors, scored at 100% of the cycle (content/references/ss_shine_footwork.json)
Which foot leads — established by comparing your whole leg pattern against the reference both ways round, with a 15.6deg margin against a 6deg noise floor (M-F-117)
notMeasured: Arm carriage and styling — MEASURED and deliberately not graded: instructors disagree by 11-58deg on arm joints in the same footwork, so there is no single correct arm to grade you against. Shown and taught, never scored (M-F-102).

Timing against the music — the beat grid for this style is unresolved (bpmStatus DISPUTED, two research passes 2x apart). Grading timing on a grid that could be doubled would blame you for our error, so no timing judgement runs until one tap measurement settles it.

Whether you truly transferred your weight — the knee-angle change this would need to detect (1.07-3.42deg across the reference's own instructors) sits inside the pipeline's own 6deg landmark-noise floor, so a verdict would be indistinguishable from tracking jitter (M-F-117).

Whether you are dancing THIS step at all — we check HOW you do the step, never WHETHER it is the step. Measured, not assumed: a hip-hop Running Man cycle and a hip-hop Bounce cycle were both judged against this reference and came back with zero errors (thigh excursion 16.9deg and 14.8deg, both under the 20deg cap that STEP_TOO_LARGE uses). So if you practise something else, this lesson will not say 'that is a different step' — it will simply find nothing wrong. A step-identity check would need its own calibration, and we have not built one.

lessons._whyUnlocked: Only step in this style with a built reference AND a proven consumer: content/references/ss_shine_footwork.json (3 attested instructors, mirrorConfident:true) is read end-to-end by tools/ss_shine_footwork_liveness.py, which shows both live errors firing on controlled corruptions and staying silent on real footage. Family's second full chain (M-F-119).

demoOnlyReason.en: We teach this one but we don't score it, and we'd rather tell you why than pretend. What makes the basic the basic is the held count — you step on 1, 2, 3 and hold on 4. To grade that we'd have to see the hold on camera, and to know what a hold looks like we'd first need footage we're certain contains one. We went looking twice: through the salsa clips we already had, then through six lessons that teach nothing but this step. Two were too short to trust, one teacher talks more than they dance, one films at an angle we can't read, and in the rest we couldn't tell a real hold from our own measurement noise. So: the step, the count, and the teaching are all here. The number isn't, until we can earn it.

lessons.evidence: steps/ss_basic.json reference.harvestProbe (pool) + harvestProbe2_targeted (6 candidates/4 harvested) + harvestProbe3_reevaluation (window fix applied, 2 independent second gates) + harvestProbe4_footLevel (ankle/heel/toe all overlap with control)

promotionPath.blockedBy: No positive control: the hold signature cannot be sought without one verified example of the basic, and that example IS the reference being sought (circular). Measured across 3 foot levels — all overlap with the shine control.
promotionPath.unblockedBy: FOUNDER, ~2 minutes: watch one candidate (FtZzjGsPxjg, 'Front & Back Basic Variations') and say whether it is the plain basic or a variation. A human eye breaks the circle that measurement cannot. If a clean basic exists in the material, the reference chain resumes and this lesson is PROMOTED demoOnly -> scored — by measurement on that day, never by opinion.
promotionPath.ifItStaysBlocked: demoOnly becomes permanent and that is an honest ending too: the step is taught, the count is taught, and no score is invented.

demoOnlyReason.en: There is no single correct arm position here — we measured it: the teachers we studied differ from each other by 11 to 58 degrees on the arms while doing the same footwork. That is style, not error. So we show you the range and let you choose; grading it would be inventing a right answer that does not exist.

lessons.evidence: content/references/ss_shine_footwork.json scoring[] — arm joints verdict coached_only / scored_partial (0-64% coverage, 11-58deg medianDispersion) while every leg joint is scored at 100%
lessons.demoOnlyClassBasis: Measured, not assumed: instructors differ 11-58deg on arm joints while doing the same footwork (M-F-102). There is no single correct arm to grade against, so no future measurement changes this — it is style, and style is the point.

whyPermanent.en: Arm styling is personal expression, not technique. There is no correct version to compare you against — scoring it would mean penalising you for having a style of your own, which is the opposite of what this lesson is for.

demoOnlyReason.en: Hearing where the music's 1 falls is the heart of salsa, and a camera cannot see whether you heard it. We teach it and leave the judging to your own ears.

lessons.evidence: plan §22 'skorlanmaz ama öğretilir' bucket — musicality/expression is explicitly outside the measurement surface, not outside the product
lessons.note: Separate from the timing block in honesty.notMeasured: that one is a solvable measurement waiting on beat_annotate; this one is not a measurement target at all.
lessons.demoOnlyClassBasis: A camera cannot hear whether you found the 1. Outside the measurement surface by nature, not by current limitation (plan §22).

whyPermanent.en: Musicality is how you hear and answer the music. A camera can see where your body is; it cannot see whether the clave is in you. This one stays taught and unscored by design, not by a gap in our data.

unlockRule.description: 3 consecutive attempts at ss_shine_footwork with shapeScore >= 0.75 and zero WRONG_FOOT
unlockRule.note: Provisional until G4 calibration (family rule M-F-04). Deliberately does NOT include onBeatRatio (no beat grid yet — bpmStatus DISPUTED) or NO_WEIGHT_TRANSFER (calibration-blocked, M-F-117): an unlock rule may only depend on judgements the app is actually allowed to make.

levels.note: Drills named by the step definitions' own error taxonomy. None of them are scored and none of them wait for a reference: a drill is a correction you practise, not a performance we judge (K10).

demoOnlyReason.en: Step and pause, and notice which foot is actually carrying you. The defining beginner habit is marking the step with the foot without ever handing the weight over — it looks close to right and feels like nothing. Slow enough that you can lift the other foot off the floor to prove where your weight went.

whyPermanent.en: What this drill teaches is a sensation — where your weight is — and that is not something a camera reads off your joint angles. You can reach the right position with your weight in the wrong place.

demoOnlyReason.en: The salsa basic is not a march: 4 is a hold, not a step. This drill is just the count with the hold exaggerated, so the gap stops feeling like a mistake you are making and starts feeling like part of the rhythm.

whyPermanent.en: This drill is about hearing the count, and hearing is not something a camera can check. We can eventually tell you whether you moved on 4; we cannot tell you whether you felt the hold.

demoOnlyReason.en: Which foot starts, and how to find it again after you lose it. Worth practising on its own because starting on the other foot does not feel wrong from the inside — everything else about the step can be correct.

whyPermanent.en: Whether you are on the 'wrong' foot depends on which foot the teacher you are following started on, and mirrored footage flips that. Until that is settled on the reference side, a score here would be a coin flip presented as a judgement.

demoOnlyReason.en: Shines travel less than beginners expect. Practise the footwork inside an imaginary square about the width of your shoulders — when the steps grow, the timing goes with them, and the fix is almost always here rather than in the count.

whyPermanent.en: How big a step should be depends on your height and your floor, and we are not going to invent a universal correct size and score you against it. The drill gives you a reference you can see; the number would be ours, not yours.

demoOnlyReason.en: The same footwork at a tempo you can actually hold, before speeding it up. Being late is usually not a timing problem — it is the step being too big or the weight arriving too late, and both are visible to you once there is time to look.

whyPermanent.en: Timing judgement needs the music's beat grid, and this drill is deliberately practised without one so you can find your own pace first. There is nothing here for us to time you against, by design.

levels.unlockRuleNote: No unlock rule by design. Every lesson in this level is a drill and none of them are scored, so there is no judgement the app is allowed to make that could gate them — an unlock rule here would have to invent a threshold on measurements we deliberately do not take (M-F-04: a rule may only depend on judgements we actually make). Drills are open from the start, which is also what they are for: you reach for one when a lesson tells you what went wrong.

referencedGenericContent.note: Harvested to chase ss_suzy_q; only 1 of the 4 sources is individually named Suzy Q, the other 3 are generic shine/footwork tutorials. Legs-only pairwise distance across all 4 (4.1-7.1 deg, best orientation) is the same order as a single reference's own instructor-to-instructor dispersion — MEASURED same-movement, not eyeballed (M-F-102 reversed an earlier visual impression that they looked different). So the id names the measured generic content, not the Suzy Q figure specifically; the Suzy Q source is tagged at source level (content/references/ss_shine_footwork.json sources[].namedVariant) rather than dropped or split out. ss_suzy_q above stays reserved and unbuilt until sourced cleanly.
